I proposed a new value for `actions.skip_stage` in the `authoring` domain. The proposal was accepted with 0 issues, and it is still waiting for a person to confirm it.

The only change is the description. It now reads: "Say a stage has nothing, in the owner's words. The owner may skip any stage, including one the tool calls required, if they write why." The old description limited the action to optional stages.

Everything else on the action is as it was. It is still owner-only and person-only. `reason` was already a required parameter, so the owner has to write why. The kernel call and the transition matrix are untouched. I left `delivery` alone because the request doesn't concern it.

The change is to the description only, so I don't know if it alters what the action actually permits. The kernel's `skip_stage` call may still refuse required stages. I didn't add a separate check that `reason` is non-empty.
